        getattr(st, level)(flash)
    try:
        bootstrap_database(path)
    except (OSError, sqlite3.Error, ValidationError, ValueError):
        st.error("The workspace database could not be initialized. Check its path and fixture data.")
        return
    tracing = initialize_tracing()
    st.caption(f"Observability · neatlogs {tracing.status.title()} — {tracing.detail}")
    _integration_status(tracing.status, tracing.detail)
    regions = list_regions(path)
    if not regions:
        st.info("No regions found. Restore the demo data from Settings.")
        return
    labels = {region.id: f"{region.name} · {region.state.value.replace('_', ' ').title()}"
              for region in regions}
    default_region = st.session_state.get("selected_region")
    if default_region not in labels:
        active_regions = [item for item in regions if item.state is RegionState.active]
        default_region = next(
            (item.id for item in active_regions if count_pending_signals(path, item.id)),
            active_regions[0].id if active_regions else regions[0].id,
        )

    section = st.radio(
        "Dashboard section",
        ["Overview", "Region operations", "Recommendations", "Activity & evidence", "Settings"],
        horizontal=True,
        label_visibility="collapsed",
        key="dashboard_section",
    )
    if section == "Overview":
        _render_overview(path, regions)
    elif section == "Region operations":
        _render_region_operations(path, regions, labels, default_region)
    selected_region = st.session_state.get("selected_region", default_region)
    if selected_region not in labels:
        selected_region = default_region
    elif section == "Recommendations":
        _render_recommendations(path, selected_region)
    elif section == "Activity & evidence":
        _render_activity(path, selected_region)
    elif section == "Settings":
        _render_settings(path)


def _integration_status(neat_status: str, neat_detail: str) -> None:
    with st.expander("Integration status", expanded=False):
        left, middle, right = st.columns(3)
        left.markdown("**neatlogs**")
        left.caption(f"{neat_status.title()} · {neat_detail}")
        middle.markdown("**cfo.ai**")
        middle.caption("Degraded · Local financial simulation; live scenario read not verified in this session.")
        right.markdown("**Entire**")
        right.caption("Checkpoint evidence is documented; entire-graph is unavailable in this environment.")


def _render_overview(path: Path, regions) -> None:
    active = [item for item in regions if item.state is RegionState.active]
    candidates = [item for item in regions if item.state is RegionState.candidate]
    latest = []
    for region in regions:
        latest.extend(list_region_cycles(path, region.id)[:1])
    latest.sort(key=lambda item: item.created_at, reverse=True)
    last_status = latest[0].status.value if latest else "No cycles yet"
    metric_cols = st.columns(4)
    metric_cols[0].metric("Active regions", len(active))
    metric_cols[1].metric("Awaiting review", len(candidates))
    metric_cols[2].metric("Latest cycle", last_status.replace("_", " ").title())
    metric_cols[3].metric("Products in catalog", len(get_product_catalog(path)))
    st.subheader("Regional portfolio")
    st.caption("Synthetic signal and commerce data · Financial and evaluation results are simulated.")
    rows = [{"Region": item.name, "Status": item.state.value.replace("_", " ").title(),
             "Locale": item.locale} for item in regions]
    st.dataframe(rows, hide_index=True, width="stretch")
    st.subheader("Latest activity")
    if latest:
        for cycle in latest[:4]:
            status = cycle.status.value.title()
            st.markdown(f"**{cycle.region_id}** · {status} · {cycle.created_at.astimezone().strftime('%b %d, %H:%M')} ")
            if cycle.rejection_reason:
                st.caption(cycle.rejection_reason.replace("_", " "))
    else:
        st.info("No autonomous cycles have run. Review a candidate or run a cycle from Region operations.")

@contextmanager
def trace(
    name: str,
    kind: Optional[str] = None,
    system_prompt_template: Optional[Union[str, "SystemPromptTemplate"]] = None,
    system_prompt_variables: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    user_prompt_template: Optional[Union[str, "UserPromptTemplate"]] = None,
    user_prompt_variables: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    prompt_template: Optional[Union[str, "SystemPromptTemplate"]] = None,
    prompt_variables: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    version: Optional[str] = None,
    capture_stdout: bool = False,
    mask: Optional[Callable] = None,
    session_id: Optional[str] = None,
    end_user_id: Optional[str] = None,
    end_user_metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    **attributes,
):
    """
    Context manager for prompt tracking and session management.

    IMPORTANT: This is NOT required for basic tracing!
    - Framework code (LangChain, OpenAI, etc.) is auto-instrumented
    - Custom code should use @span(kind="...") decorator

    Use trace() ONLY for:
    1. Prompt template tracking (captures template + variables for versioning)
    2. Multi-turn session management (groups turns within a session)
    3. Grouping multiple top-level operations in main()

    **When NOT to use trace():**
    - Don't wrap a single @span(kind="WORKFLOW") call - it's already traced!
    - Don't use for custom functions - use @span(kind="...") decorator instead
    - Don't use just to "create a span" - auto-instrumentation handles that

    **Session-Aware Trace Creation:**
    - If `session_id` is set in init() AND no active parent span exists,
      this creates a NEW root trace (for multi-turn conversations).
    - Otherwise, creates a normal child span within the existing trace.

    Args:
        name: Span name
        kind: OpenInference span kind (rarely needed - auto-inferred)
        system_prompt_template: SystemPromptTemplate object for system prompt versioning
        system_prompt_variables: Dict of system prompt variables (legacy string templates only)
        user_prompt_template: UserPromptTemplate object for user/human prompt versioning
        user_prompt_variables: Dict of user prompt variables (legacy string templates only)
        prompt_template: Deprecated alias for ``system_prompt_template``. Kept for
            backward compat; new code should use ``system_prompt_template``.
        prompt_variables: Deprecated alias for ``system_prompt_variables``.
        version: Optional version identifier
        end_user_id: Identifier of the END-USER this trace belongs to — i.e. the
            user of your application, not the operator running the SDK. One
            end-user per trace; the backend rolls this up to the trace and its
            session for filtering/analytics. Distinct from init(user_id=...).
        end_user_metadata: Optional dict of arbitrary end-user fields
            (e.g. {"plan": "pro", "email": "a@b.com"}), stored as JSON on the trace.
        **attributes: Additional attributes to set on the span

    Examples:

        Use Case 1: Prompt template tracking (inside your function):

        >>> template = SystemPromptTemplate([{"role": "user", "content": "{{query}}"}])
        >>>
        >>> @span(kind="AGENT")
        >>> def my_agent(query: str):
        ...     with trace(name="prompt", system_prompt_template=template):
        ...         messages = template.compile(query=query)  # Compile ONCE
        ...         response = llm.create(messages=messages)   # No duplication!
        ...     return response

        Use Case 2: Multi-turn sessions:

        >>> neatlogs.init(api_key="...", session_id="user-123")
        >>>
        >>> with trace(name="turn_1"):  # New root trace (same session)
        ...     agent.run("Hello")
        >>>
        >>> with trace(name="turn_2"):  # New root trace (same session)
        ...     agent.run("Tell me more")

        Use Case 3: Grouping multiple operations in main:

        >>> def main():
        ...     with trace(name="pipeline"):  # Groups multiple steps
        ...         step1()  # @span(kind="CHAIN")
        ...         step2()  # @span(kind="CHAIN")

"""Operator utilities for synthetic evidence and a repeatable demo reset."""

import hashlib
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from uuid import uuid4

from adaptive_commerce.domain import Signal, SignalSourceType
from adaptive_commerce.persistence import Repository, connect, load_fixtures

FIXTURES = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "data" / "fixtures"


def inject_demo_signal(
    path: Path,
    region_id: str,
    topics: list[str],
    confidence: float,
    evidence: str,
    source_type: SignalSourceType = SignalSourceType.social,
    observed_at: datetime | None = None,
) -> Signal:
    """Persist one idempotent synthetic signal for an operator demonstration.

    Identical region, source type, topic, confidence, and evidence inputs reuse
    the same source record. Change the evidence text to model a distinct report.
    """
    with connect(path) as conn:
        repository = Repository(conn)
        region = repository.get_region(region_id)
        if region is None:
            raise ValueError("selected region does not exist")
        normalized_topics = sorted({topic.strip().lower() for topic in topics if topic.strip()})
        normalized_evidence = " ".join(evidence.split())
        identity = json.dumps({
            "region_id": region_id,
            "source_type": source_type.value,
            "topics": normalized_topics,
            "confidence": str(confidence),
            "evidence": normalized_evidence.casefold(),
        }, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
        source_id = f"demo:{hashlib.sha256(identity.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()}"
        existing = repository.get_signals_by_source_id(source_id)
        if existing:
            return existing[0]
        signal = Signal(
            id=f"signal:{uuid4().hex}",
            region_id=region_id,
            source_id=source_id,
            source_type=source_type,
            topics=normalized_topics,
            confidence=confidence,
            observed_at=observed_at or datetime.now(timezone.utc),
            evidence_excerpt=normalized_evidence,
            language="en",
            normalized_text=normalized_evidence,
        )
        if not repository.create_signal(signal):
            return repository.get_signals_by_source_id(source_id)[0]
        return signal


def reset_demo(path: Path) -> None:
    """Clear local application state and restore the checked-in synthetic fixtures."""
    with connect(path) as conn:
        conn.execute("PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys = ON")
        for table in (
            "evidence_references", "recommendation_items", "consumed_signals", "signals", "source_records",
            "event_windows", "finance_assessments", "operator_actions", "update_cycles",
            "simulated_events", "region_profiles", "recommendation_versions", "regions",
            "products",
        ):
            conn.execute(f"DELETE FROM {table}")
        load_fixtures(conn, FIXTURES)

from contextlib import contextmanager

from adaptive_commerce.integrations import observability


def test_trace_step_records_workflow_ids_without_capturing_payload(monkeypatch):
    recorded = {"attributes": {}, "name": None, "kind": None}

    class Span:
        def set_attribute(self, name, value):
            recorded["attributes"][name] = value

    @contextmanager
    def fake_trace(name, *, kind):
        recorded["name"] = name
        recorded["kind"] = kind
        yield Span()

    monkeypatch.setattr(observability.neatlogs, "trace", fake_trace)

    with observability.trace_step(
        "CHAIN", "recommendation_ranking", region_id="r1",
        cycle_id="c1", version_id="v1",
    ):
        pass

    assert recorded == {
        "name": "recommendation_ranking",
        "kind": "CHAIN",
        "attributes": {
            "atlas.region_id": "r1",
            "atlas.cycle_id": "c1",
            "atlas.version_id": "v1",
        },
    }


def test_trace_step_preserves_workflow_errors(monkeypatch):
    @contextmanager
    def fake_trace(*_args, **_kwargs):
        yield object()

    monkeypatch.setattr(observability.neatlogs, "trace", fake_trace)

    try:
        with observability.trace_step("AGENT", "signal_extraction"):
            raise RuntimeError("signal extraction failed")
    except RuntimeError as error:
        assert str(error) == "signal extraction failed"
    else:
        raise AssertionError("trace_step must not swallow workflow failures")

def test_trace_step_records_workflow_ids_without_capturing_payload(monkeypatch):
    recorded = {"attributes": {}, "name": None, "kind": None}

# Installing uv

## Installation methods

Install uv with our standalone installers or your package manager of choice.

### Standalone installer

uv provides a standalone installer to download and install uv:

[Input][Input]

macOS and Linux Windows

Use `curl` to download the script and execute it with `sh`:
    
    `$ curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
    `

If your system doesn't have `curl`, you can use `wget`:
    
    `$ wget -qO- https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
    `

Request a specific version by including it in the URL:
    
    `$ curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/0.13.0/install.sh | sh
    `

Use `irm` to download the script and execute it with `iex`:
    
    `PS> powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
    `

Changing the execution policy allows running a script from the internet.

Request a specific version by including it in the URL:
    
    `PS> powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/0.13.0/install.ps1 | iex"
    `

Tip

The installation script may be inspected before use:

[Input][Input]

macOS and Linux Windows
    
    `$ curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | less
    `
    
    `PS> powershell -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | more"
    `

Alternatively, the installer or binaries can be downloaded directly from GitHub.

See the reference documentation on the installer for details on customizing your uv installation.

### PyPI

For convenience, uv is published to PyPI.

If installing from PyPI, we recommend installing uv into an isolated environment, e.g., with `pipx`:
    
    `$ pipx install uv
    `

However, `pip` can also be used:
    
    `$ pip install uv
    `

Note

uv ships with prebuilt distributions (wheels) for many platforms; if a wheel is not available for a given platform, uv will be built from source, which requires a Rust toolchain. See the contributing setup guide for details on building uv from source.

### Homebrew

uv is available in the core Homebrew packages.
    
    `$ brew install uv
    `

### MacPorts

uv is available via MacPorts.
    
    `$ sudo port install uv
    `

### WinGet

uv is available via WinGet.
    
    `$ winget install --id=astral-sh.uv  -e
    `

### Scoop

uv is available via Scoop.
    
    `$ scoop install main/uv
    `

### Docker

uv provides a Docker image at `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv`.

See our guide on using uv in Docker for more details.

### GitHub Releases

uv release artifacts can be downloaded directly from GitHub Releases.

Each release page includes binaries for all supported platforms as well as instructions for using the standalone installer via `github.com` instead of `astral.sh`.

### Cargo

uv is available via crates.io.
    
    `$ cargo install --locked uv
    `

Then restart the shell or source the shell config file.

## Uninstallation

If you need to remove uv from your system, follow these steps:

  1. Clean up stored data (optional):
    
    `$ uv cache clean
    $ rm -r "$(uv python dir)"
    $ rm -r "$(uv tool dir)"
    `

Tip

Before removing the binaries, you may want to remove any data that uv has stored. See the storage reference for details on where uv stores data.

  2. Remove the uv, uvx, and uvw binaries:

[Input][Input]

macOS and Linux Windows
    
    `$ rm ~/.local/bin/uv ~/.local/bin/uvx
    `
    
    `PS> rm $HOME\.local\bin\uv.exe
    PS> rm $HOME\.local\bin\uvx.exe
    PS> rm $HOME\.local\bin\uvw.exe
    `

Note

Prior to 0.5.0, uv was installed into `~/.cargo/bin`. The binaries can be removed from there to uninstall. Upgrading from an older version will not automatically remove the binaries from `~/.cargo/bin`.

# Python SDK

Install, initialize, and instrument Python LLM and agent apps with Neatlogs.

The Python SDK installs from PyPI as `neatlogs`. Use the latest published stable release. Wrap the AI clients you already use, add spans to your own functions, and track prompt templates — every call is captured as a trace in your dashboard. This page covers everything from install to the full `init()` reference; use the contents on the right to jump around.

Note

New to tracing? A trace is the record of one run of your app; a span is one step inside it (an LLM call, a tool call). You instrument once, then read traces in the dashboard. See Introduction.

## Install

To auto-instrument a specific library, install its extra (same `-U` rule applies):
    
    `pip install -U "neatlogs[openai]"      # OpenAI

    pip install -U "neatlogs[langchain]"   # LangChain / LangGraph
See SDK Doctor for the full pass criteria, reason codes, and safe troubleshooting steps.

## Your first trace

Call `neatlogs.init()` once, then wrap your AI client with `neatlogs.wrap(...)`. From then on every call that client makes is recorded — you use the client exactly as before.

Note

EU projects: add `endpoint="https://eu.ingest.neatlogs.com"` to `neatlogs.init(...)`. Use the base URL, without `/v1/traces`.
    
    `neatlogs.init(

## Log capture

Log capture is opt-in — pass `capture_logs=True` to `init()`. Neatlogs then records logs as `LOG` spans (children of the active span) so they appear inline in the trace timeline. Without it, none of the three mechanisms below capture anything.
    
    `neatlogs.init(api_key="...", capture_logs=True)
    
    @neatlogs.span(kind="CHAIN")

        docs = retrieve(query)
        neatlogs.log("retrieved {count} docs", count=len(docs))
        return generate(query, docs)`

    `import neatlogs
    
    # Caller — inject before sending. Returns False (carrier untouched) if no span is active.
    with neatlogs.trace("caller"):
        headers = {"content-type": "application/json"}
        if neatlogs.inject_trace_context(headers):
            requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload)
    
    # Callee — extract to continue the trace. Re-bind identity here (it does NOT ride the wire).
    with neatlogs.extract_trace_context(
        req.headers,
        session_id=sid,
        parent_session_id=parent_sid,
        session_custom_fields={"feature_name": feature, "entry_point": "api"},

The dashboard is ready to run with Neatlogs enabled. I updated startup so it loads `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` from the repository’s ignored `.env` file; a value exported in your shell takes precedence. The regional cycle now traces signal fetching, policy checks, ranking, evaluation, activation or rejection, and retries. Traces include workflow IDs, counts, and outcomes, but not evidence text. See [observability setup](/Users/suryaanshs/Desktop/neathack/atlas-commerce-maxxed/src/adaptive_commerce/integrations/observability.py:26) and [cycle tracing](/Users/suryaanshs/Desktop/neathack/atlas-commerce-maxxed/src/adaptive_commerce/application/worker.py:73).

## Start it on your Mac

If `uv` is still missing, install it with Homebrew and restart your terminal: `brew install uv`. ([uv installation guide](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/))

Then, from the repo directory:

```bash
uv sync --locked
uv run streamlit run app.py
```

The app loads the existing local `.env` automatically. Keep that file private; don’t commit it. The startup and Neatlogs commands are also in the [README](/Users/suryaanshs/Desktop/neathack/atlas-commerce-maxxed/README.md:76).

## Follow a workflow and see its traces

In the dashboard, choose a region, add synthetic evidence, then run a regional cycle. The cycle evaluates the proposed recommendations and either activates a new version or preserves the current one. Open Neatlogs and look for the `atlas-commerce` workflow; use the region and cycle IDs to find the corresponding steps.

To run the background worker instead, use `uv run python worker.py --once`. For scheduled runs, use `uv run python worker.py --interval 300`. Use one cycle runner at a time—the dashboard or the worker—to avoid competing runs on the same local database.

I verified the Neatlogs connection with `uv run python -m neatlogs doctor --probe --json`: the diagnostic trace was visible and finalized. I also ran a synthetic Cedar cycle; it activated and the SDK flush completed. **The exact app trace has not yet been read back through the CLI**: that command also needs `NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID` and `NEATLOGS_TOKEN`, which aren’t configured here. The evidence and trace ID are recorded in [docs/evidence.md](/Users/suryaanshs/Desktop/neathack/atlas-commerce-maxxed/docs/evidence.md:28). ([Neatlogs Python SDK guide](https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/python))

The full test suite passes: **152 tests**. Neatlogs records the application workflow; it does not provide the LLM itself. cfo.ai and Entire also remain separate integrations with their own setup and verification requirements.

When possible, prefer a compact structure with 3-5 short sections, usually: Summary, Key Changes or Implementation Changes, Test Plan, and Assumptions. Do not include a separate Scope section unless scope boundaries are genuinely important to avoid mistakes.

Prefer grouped implementation bullets by subsystem or behavior over file-by-file inventories. Mention files only when needed to disambiguate a non-obvious change, and avoid naming more than 3 paths unless extra specificity is necessary to prevent mistakes. Prefer behavior-level descriptions over symbol-by-symbol removal lists. For v1 feature-addition plans, do not invent detailed schema, validation, precedence, fallback, or wire-shape policy unless the request establishes it or it is needed to prevent a concrete implementation mistake; prefer the intended capability and minimum interface/behavior changes.

Keep bullets short and avoid explanatory sub-bullets unless they are needed to prevent ambiguity. Prefer the minimum detail needed for implementation safety, not exhaustive coverage. Within each section, compress related changes into a few high-signal bullets and omit branch-by-branch logic, repeated invariants, and long lists of unaffected behavior unless they are necessary to prevent a likely implementation mistake. Only produce at most one `<proposed_plan>` block per turn, and only when you are presenting a complete spec.

If the user stays in Plan mode and asks for revisions after a prior `<proposed_plan>`, any new `<proposed_plan>` must be a complete replacement. If the follow-up neither requires changes nor calls the plan into question (e.g. clarifying question), answer it before the block, then reproduce the prior `<proposed_plan>` unchanged.

# Atlas Commerce Agent — Integration Contract

The hackathon requires meaningful use of neatlogs, Entire, and cfo.ai. This document defines what counts as implementation and what evidence must be captured.

## Integration interaction model

The following UML sequence shows how the application uses all three products across development, runtime, and business planning:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor Developer
    participant Agent as Coding agent
    participant Entire
    participant App as Atlas Commerce
    participant Neat as neatlogs
    participant CFO as cfo.ai MCP

    Developer->>Agent: Implement or improve workflow
    Agent->>Entire: Query repository context
    Entire-->>Agent: Graph, history, and prior decisions
    Agent->>App: Write code and tests
    Agent->>Entire: Save checkpoint with session context

    App->>Neat: Trace region assessment/update workflow
    App->>CFO: Read or create financial scenario
    CFO-->>App: Revenue, cost, margin, ROI, and viability outputs
    App->>Neat: Record finance decision and recommendation version
    App->>App: Activate, reject, or roll back update
    App->>Neat: Record result, failure, retry, and evaluation metrics

    Developer->>Entire: Inspect checkpoint evidence
    Developer->>Neat: Inspect trace and before/after evaluation
    Developer->>CFO: Inspect business model and scenarios
```

## neatlogs

### Role

neatlogs is the runtime observability and evaluation layer. It must show how an autonomous cycle worked, what changed, whether it failed, and whether a fix improved the result.

### Required implementation

- initialize the Python SDK once;
- wrap the LLM client when an LLM is used;
- trace the top-level region update workflow;
- trace each research agent and tool call;
- trace source ingestion, policy guardrails, ranking, evaluation, and activation;
- attach region ID, cycle ID, recommendation version, and result status;
- record errors and bounded retries;
- record evaluation metrics for active versus candidate versions;
- query or link the relevant trace/evaluation in the dashboard.

### Required evidence

Capture:

1. a successful candidate-region assessment cycle;
2. a successful autonomous update cycle where recommendations change;
3. a failed or rejected update showing what the system did next;
4. before/after evaluation values;
5. trace IDs or screenshots for the demo and repository.

The neatlogs Python SDK supports custom spans for workflows, agents, tools, guardrails, and retrieval steps. Its public API can read traces and automate workflows when the project has suitable credentials and access. Verify the authenticated connection before building logic that depends on API reads. [Python SDK](https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/python) · [Public API](https://docs.neatlogs.com/api-reference)

## Entire

### Role

Entire supplies repository context and records coding-agent work. It is a development and change-history integration for this project.

### Required implementation

- install/configure Entire for the project repository;
- use repository context or `entire-graph` while implementing the orchestrator and integrations;
- keep this `AGENTS.md` and the planning documents available to the coding agent;
- create a checkpoint after the core workflow is implemented;
- create a second checkpoint after an evidence-backed improvement or failure recovery fix;
- record the checkpoint/commit references in the submission evidence.

The application must not claim that ordinary runtime weight updates are Entire code changes. Runtime profiles are versioned in SQLite; code or agent-instruction changes are captured by Entire.

Entire describes checkpoints as code changes paired with the prompt, reasoning, and tool calls behind them, and provides repository/session search and semantic graph context. [Entire documentation](https://docs.entire.io/)

## cfo.ai

### Role

cfo.ai is the business and financial model layer. It determines whether opening a region is economically worthwhile and models the business around the agent.

### Required implementation

Create a cfo.ai model with:

- active regions and candidate regions;
- monthly or weekly traffic;
- conversion rate;
- average order value;
- product and fulfillment costs;
- inference and infrastructure cost;
- customer acquisition or campaign cost;
- revenue, gross profit, gross margin, and runway;
- base, growth, and downside scenarios;
- regional opportunity cost;
- product or campaign ROI.

The application should submit or read a regional scenario through the cfo.ai MCP connection where access is available. It must store references to the model and scenario, display the returned outputs, and convert approved thresholds into a local `FinancePolicy` used by the activation and ranking services.

If MCP authentication or an operation is unavailable, the UI must state `cfo.ai unavailable` and show that the assessment is a local fallback. The demo may continue, but the cfo.ai integration is not considered complete until a real model/scenario read is verified.

cfo.ai documents a remote MCP server at `https://api.cfo.ai/mcp` that can inspect and, with authorization, modify models, scenarios, variables, pages, and formulas. Its scenario workflow supports alternative plans while keeping the main model unchanged. [MCP setup](https://docs.cfo.ai/integrations/mcp-server) · [Scenario documentation](https://docs.cfo.ai/scenarios/create-and-compare-scenarios)

### Required evidence

- cfo.ai model link or workspace reference;
- regional viability scenario;
- base/growth/downside comparison;
- business plan for pricing, costs, revenue, and runway;
- screenshot or export of the financial outputs used by the demo;
- mapping from cfo.ai outputs to the application's activation policy.

## Evidence manifest

Create `docs/evidence.md` during implementation with:

```text
neatlogs project:
neatlogs successful trace:
neatlogs failed/rejected trace:
neatlogs evaluation:
Entire repository/checkpoint:
Entire graph output:
cfo.ai workspace/model:
cfo.ai scenario:
cfo.ai business plan:
```

Do not put secrets or private customer data in the evidence manifest.
# Atlas Commerce Agent — Architecture

## Design principles

The system is a modular monolith with durable state and clear integration adapters. Domain decisions should be testable without a UI, LLM, or network connection. External integrations must report unavailable, degraded, or successful status explicitly.

The prototype uses a deterministic weighted ranker and synthetic streams. This gives us visible, repeatable recommendation changes while preserving extension points for real data and more advanced models later.

## High-level flow

```text
Streamlit dashboard
        |
Application services
        |
Region lifecycle service ---- Financial viability service ---- cfo.ai MCP
        |
Autonomous worker
        |
Signal ingestion → research/normalization → policy guardrail
        |                                      |
        +→ candidate weight update → evaluator → activation/rollback
        |
Recommendation service → product ranking → storefront preview
        |
SQLite state and version history
        |
neatlogs traces/evaluations       Entire development context/checkpoints
```

## Components

### Presentation layer

Streamlit provides the demo dashboard. It displays region states, finance assessments, signals, rankings, update proposals, and evidence. It calls application services and does not contain ranking or integration logic.

### Region lifecycle service

Responsibilities:

- register candidate regions;
- request viability assessment;
- store assessment results;
- activate or reject a region after human approval;
- pause, resume, or archive a region;
- expose the current lifecycle state.

### Autonomous worker

The worker runs a polling cycle over active regions. In demo mode, a button or accelerated clock triggers the same cycle. Each cycle is idempotent and records a cycle ID.

The worker must isolate failures by region. It processes only new signal IDs, skips stale or low-confidence evidence, and never replaces the active recommendation version until the candidate passes validation.

### Research and normalization agents

The agents read synthetic source records and produce structured `RegionalSignal` objects:

- source ID and source type;
- region ID;
- observed timestamp;
- extracted topics/tags;
- sentiment or demand direction;
- confidence;
- evidence excerpt;
- language and normalized text;
- event window when relevant.

The LLM is optional for fixture mode. The application must have a deterministic extractor so tests and the demo remain reproducible.

### Policy guardrail

The guardrail removes products that violate explicit product, inventory, regional, or campaign rules. It also checks that signals do not contain unsupported sensitive targeting assumptions.

### Recommendation service

The service loads the active `RegionProfile`, `Product` records, active events, and eligible policies. It computes scores, returns ranked products, and stores the score breakdown for explanation.

### Update and evaluation service

The update service creates a candidate profile from newly observed signals. It clamps changes, attaches evidence, and creates a candidate version. The evaluation service compares active and candidate profiles against the same simulated customer cohort and calculates relevance, conversion, contribution profit, policy violations, and ranking movement.

The candidate is activated only when it meets configured thresholds. Otherwise it is rejected and the active version remains unchanged.

The autonomous update is represented as a UML sequence model:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Worker as Autonomous worker
    participant Source as Signal source
    participant Research as Research agents
    participant Guard as Policy guardrail
    participant Ranker as Recommendation service
    participant Eval as Evaluation service
    participant Finance as Finance policy
    participant DB as SQLite repository
    participant Logs as neatlogs

    Worker->>Logs: Open WORKFLOW cycle
    Worker->>Source: Fetch unseen records
    Source-->>Worker: Timestamped source records
    Worker->>Research: Extract topics and evidence
    Research-->>Worker: Normalized regional signals
    Worker->>Guard: Validate signal and product policies
    Guard-->>Worker: Eligible update inputs
    Worker->>Ranker: Create bounded candidate profile
    Ranker->>DB: Load active profile and catalog
    DB-->>Ranker: Active weights and products
    Ranker-->>Worker: Candidate ranking and explanations
    Worker->>Eval: Compare active and candidate versions
    Eval-->>Worker: Quality, profit, and ranking metrics
    Worker->>Finance: Check financial constraints
    Finance-->>Worker: Pass or reject
    alt All checks pass
        Worker->>DB: Transactionally activate candidate version
        Worker->>Logs: Record activation and before/after results
    else Any check fails
        Worker->>DB: Preserve active version
        Worker->>Logs: Record rejection or rollback
    end
```

### Financial viability service

The service builds a structured regional assessment from traffic, conversion, order value, margin, fulfillment, campaign, and inference assumptions. It sends or exposes scenario inputs through the cfo.ai adapter, records the returned model/scenario references and outputs, and applies a local decision policy.

The local policy is needed for deterministic application behavior even when cfo.ai is unavailable. It must clearly indicate when it used a fallback calculation.

## Domain objects

- `Region`: identity, lifecycle state, locale, source availability, and timestamps.
- `RegionProfile`: region weights, policy version, active recommendation version, and update limits.
- `Product`: catalog metadata, tags, cost, price, stock, and eligibility.
- `Signal`: normalized evidence extracted from a source record.
- `EventWindow`: temporary topic boosts with start and expiry timestamps.
- `FinanceAssessment`: assumptions, scenarios, score, decision, and cfo.ai references.
- `RecommendationVersion`: immutable weight snapshot and parent version.
- `RecommendationItem`: product score and score breakdown for a version.
- `UpdateCycle`: input signal IDs, proposed changes, evaluation, result, and error state.
- `EvidenceReference`: neatlogs trace/evaluation, Entire checkpoint, or cfo.ai scenario reference.

The core domain relationships are represented as a UML class model:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Region {
        +UUID id
        +String name
        +RegionState state
        +String locale
    }
    class RegionProfile {
        +UUID region_id
        +Map weights
        +UUID active_version_id
        +Decimal max_weight_delta
    }
    class Product {
        +UUID id
        +String name
        +List tags
        +Decimal price
        +Decimal cost
        +Boolean in_stock
    }
    class Signal {
        +UUID id
        +UUID region_id
        +String source_type
        +List topics
        +Decimal confidence
        +DateTime observed_at
    }
    class EventWindow {
        +UUID id
        +DateTime starts_at
        +DateTime expires_at
        +Map boosts
    }
    class FinanceAssessment {
        +UUID id
        +Decimal viability_score
        +Decimal projected_profit
        +String decision
        +String cfo_reference
    }
    class RecommendationVersion {
        +UUID id
        +UUID parent_id
        +Map weights
        +String status
    }
    class UpdateCycle {
        +UUID id
        +String status
        +String rejection_reason
        +String neatlogs_trace_id
    }

    Region "1" *-- "1" RegionProfile
    Region "1" o-- "many" Signal
    Region "1" o-- "many" EventWindow
    Region "1" o-- "many" FinanceAssessment
    RegionProfile "1" --> "many" RecommendationVersion
    RecommendationVersion "1" --> "many" Product : ranks
    UpdateCycle "many" --> "1" Region
    UpdateCycle "many" --> "many" Signal : consumes
    UpdateCycle "1" --> "1" RecommendationVersion : proposes
    FinanceAssessment "1" --> "1" Region
```

## Persistence

SQLite is the source of truth for the prototype. Store immutable versions rather than overwriting weights. Use transactions for activation and rollback.

Suggested tables:

```text
regions
region_profiles
products
source_records
signals
event_windows
finance_assessments
recommendation_versions
recommendation_items
update_cycles
evidence_references
simulated_events
```

## Integration boundaries

### neatlogs adapter

Initialize once at process startup. Decorate the top-level cycle as a `WORKFLOW`; use `AGENT`, `TOOL`, `GUARDRAIL`, `RETRIEVER`, and `CHAIN` spans for the corresponding steps. Include region ID, cycle ID, model version, and result status as attributes. Capture failures, retries, latency, token usage, and evaluation results.

The adapter must support a local no-network mode for unit tests, but the demo must run with the real project key and produce inspectable traces.

### cfo.ai adapter

Provide operations for creating/reading a regional scenario and reading calculated outputs. Prefer the cfo.ai MCP server for the authenticated workspace. Preserve workspace, model, scenario, and page references in `EvidenceReference` records.

The adapter must expose `connected`, `degraded`, and `failed` states. Do not call a local fallback result a cfo.ai result.

### Entire evidence

Entire is a development integration. Use it with the repository and coding agent to inspect code context, create checkpoints for meaningful improvements, and generate `entire-graph` evidence where useful. The application may store a human-readable checkpoint URL or commit reference in the evidence table, but runtime recommendation updates remain application data.

## Extension points

The following interfaces should be small and replaceable:

- `SignalSource`: replace fixtures with RSS, news, forum, or approved API sources.
- `SignalExtractor`: replace deterministic extraction with multilingual LLM extraction.
- `RecommendationScorer`: replace weighted ranking with a learned model.
- `EvaluationStrategy`: replace the simulator with offline replay or A/B measurements.
- `FinanceProvider`: replace the prototype adapter with a verified cfo.ai MCP client.
- `Scheduler`: replace accelerated polling with a production job runner.
- `StateRepository`: replace SQLite with PostgreSQL when multi-user concurrency requires it.
# Atlas Commerce Agent — Product Definition

## Product statement

Atlas Commerce is an autonomous regional expansion and recommendation system. It evaluates whether a new region is financially worth serving, waits for human approval to activate it, and then adapts that region's product recommendations as new regional signals arrive.

The prototype uses synthetic data streams and a simulated storefront. It demonstrates the control loop that could later consume real commerce, news, event, and community data.

## User and primary workflow

The primary user is a commerce operator or product manager.

The user submits a candidate region with a name, market assumptions, and an optional event or launch context. The system gathers the region's available signals, estimates financial viability, and presents a recommendation to approve or reject activation.

After approval, the region enters an active state. The autonomous worker periodically processes new signals, proposes a bounded weight update, validates its effect on recommendations and simulated economics, and activates or rejects the update. The user does not need to approve routine weight updates, but can pause a region or restore an earlier version.

## What the user should see

The dashboard should make the following visible:

- candidate and active regions;
- financial viability score and supporting assumptions;
- current region profile and active recommendation version;
- incoming signals and their evidence;
- product recommendations before and after an update;
- products promoted, demoted, added, and removed;
- explanation for each score change;
- update status, confidence, and rollback status;
- neatlogs trace/evaluation links or IDs;
- Entire checkpoint/evidence references;
- cfo.ai scenario and model references.

## Recommendation behavior

The catalog contains products with tags, price, cost, stock, base popularity, and policy eligibility. A region has weights for interests such as `outdoor`, `travel`, `festival`, and `electronics`.

The initial ranker is deterministic:

```text
score = base_popularity
      + regional_interest_match
      + temporary_event_boost
      + margin_bonus
      - policy_penalty
```

LLM agents may extract normalized signals from text, but a deterministic scorer produces the final ranking. Weight changes are bounded, versioned, and reversible.

The demo must show a clear ranking change. For example, a region initially recommends hiking products; a new festival signal increases festival and electronics weights; portable chargers, phone pouches, and festival accessories move into the top five.

## Region lifecycle

```text
candidate → assessing → awaiting_approval → active
                                      ↘ rejected
active → monitoring → update_candidate → active
                              ↘ rejected/rolled_back
active → paused → active
active → archived
```

Only activation of a new region requires human approval. The system can autonomously process routine updates for active regions. A global pause and a per-region pause remain available for recovery.

The lifecycle is represented as a UML state machine:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> candidate
    candidate --> assessing: submit region
    assessing --> awaiting_approval: finance assessment ready
    assessing --> rejected: insufficient data or viability
    awaiting_approval --> active: human approves
    awaiting_approval --> rejected: human rejects
    active --> monitoring: autonomous cycle
    monitoring --> update_candidate: new usable signals
    monitoring --> monitoring: no actionable change
    update_candidate --> active: evaluation passes
    update_candidate --> rejected_update: policy, finance, or quality failure
    rejected_update --> active: preserve active version
    active --> paused: operator pause or emergency stop
    paused --> active: operator resumes
    active --> archived: region retired
    rejected --> [*]
    archived --> [*]
```

The primary user interaction and autonomous update are shown below as a UML sequence model:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor Operator
    participant UI as Dashboard
    participant Lifecycle as Region service
    participant Finance as cfo.ai adapter
    participant Worker as Autonomous worker
    participant Ranker as Recommendation service
    participant Store as Versioned state
    participant Logs as neatlogs

    Operator->>UI: Submit candidate region
    UI->>Lifecycle: Create assessment
    Lifecycle->>Finance: Evaluate scenarios and viability
    Finance-->>Lifecycle: Score, scenarios, and references
    Lifecycle-->>UI: Show approval decision
    Operator->>UI: Approve region
    UI->>Lifecycle: Activate region
    Worker->>Logs: Start autonomous cycle trace
    Worker->>Ranker: Rank with active weights
    Worker->>Worker: Ingest and normalize new signal
    Worker->>Ranker: Create candidate weights
    Ranker->>Store: Compare active and candidate rankings
    alt Candidate passes checks
        Worker->>Store: Activate new version
        Worker->>Logs: Record changed recommendations
    else Candidate fails checks
        Worker->>Store: Preserve active version
        Worker->>Logs: Record rejection and reason
    end
```

## Safety and quality boundaries

- Use explicit product and regional exclusion policies.
- Do not infer sensitive customer or political attributes.
- Require sufficient signal confidence and minimum evidence before an update.
- Clamp weight changes and limit the number of changes per cycle.
- Expire temporary event boosts automatically.
- Do not recommend unavailable or disallowed products.
- Reject an update when its evaluation is worse than the active version.
- Preserve the last known-good version.
- Label all synthetic data and simulated business results in the UI and demo.

## Hackathon scope

### Included in the prototype

- one shared synthetic product catalog;
- two already active regions;
- one candidate region;
- synthetic news, forum, social, and event streams;
- financial viability assessment;
- human region activation;
- autonomous signal processing and bounded weight updates;
- before/after product recommendations;
- simulated impressions, clicks, orders, ratings, and profit;
- neatlogs runtime traces and evaluations;
- Entire development checkpoints and repository context evidence;
- cfo.ai business model and regional scenarios;
- failure, rejection, and rollback demonstrations.

### Deferred for later improvements

- production feeds and source authentication;
- real multilingual translation and source credibility models;
- collaborative or neural recommendation models;
- real A/B experimentation and causal measurement;
- inventory, payments, fulfillment, and return integrations;
- distributed workers and production deployment;
- automated code changes generated at runtime;
- identity, access control, and multi-tenant administration;
- model training pipelines and feature stores.

## Success criteria

The prototype succeeds when a reviewer can start with a candidate region, understand its financial decision, approve it, run an autonomous data cycle, see its top products change, inspect why they changed, observe the run in neatlogs, verify the development history through Entire, and inspect the financial assumptions in cfo.ai.

### Recovery pass — October 10, 2026, after the published Sprint 1 window

The user explicitly authorized Ad's coding agent to complete the remaining Z,
Ar, and S Sprint 1 work after the foundation review. This recovery pass stays
on the existing `feat/s1-ad-ranking-core` branch / PR #3 to preserve its pending
public API changes. This is an explicit cross-owner completion exception;
normal ownership resumes for Sprint 2. No other task branches are overwritten.
The original four-sprint sequence remains unchanged; subsequent sprint start
times must be re-baselined by the team after this recovery PR is reviewed.
Do not interpret the original timestamps or unchecked central table as live
completion evidence. Current verification and named blockers are maintained in
`docs/evidence.md`; no merge/reviewer box is checked by the implementation agent.

This plan preserves the four-sprint sequence for the consolidated fork implementation requested on October 10. The published sprint window had elapsed, so its timestamps are re-baselined below; task order, acceptance criteria, ownership labels, and merge gates remain in force.

- **Date:** Saturday, October 10, 2026
- **Timezone:** India Standard Time (IST, UTC+05:30)
- **Re-baselined window:** `2026-10-10 21:30` through `2026-10-11 03:30 IST`
- **Sprint duration:** Four 90-minute sprints
- **Team:** Z, Ar, Ad, and S

The team works in parallel within each sprint. At each sprint boundary, S coordinates integration, review, and the next sprint's branch cut. Each contributor owns the files for their assigned slice. If work depends on a teammate's unfinished interface, use the contract in `ARCHITECTURE.md` and a small local stub; do not edit the other person's files.

## Team ownership

| Teammate | Primary ownership | Typical files |
|---|---|---|
| **Z** | Domain schemas, SQLite persistence, version history, transactions | `src/adaptive_commerce/domain/`, `src/adaptive_commerce/persistence/`, persistence tests |
| **Ar** | Streamlit screens, user flow, storefront preview, demo usability | `src/adaptive_commerce/presentation/`, `app.py`, UI tests |
| **Ad** | Agent workflow, signal processing, recommendation logic, worker, evaluation | `src/adaptive_commerce/agents/`, `application/`, `recommender/`, `worker.py`, logic tests |
| **S** | neatlogs/cfo.ai integration, integration test coordination, evidence, sprint integration | `src/adaptive_commerce/integrations/`, `docs/evidence.md`, integration tests |

S is the integration steward. Each task owner updates their own GitHub PR checklist. S alone updates the central sprint status boxes after confirming the PR exists and the required checks are green; this avoids concurrent edits to the shared sprint tracker.

## Branch and GitHub workflow

- Create the task branch shown below from the current `main` at the sprint start.

- Use a short imperative commit subject, such as `Add bounded regional weight updates`.
- Open a pull request to `main` before the sprint end. Add the sprint label and link the exact task.
- The task owner ticks **PR uploaded and checks passed** only after pushing the branch, adding its PR URL, and seeing the required checks pass.
- The task owner leaves **reviewed and merged** for S/reviewer to tick after review and merge.
- S updates the central task checkbox after confirming the PR URL and green checks. A push without tests or a PR does not complete a checklist item.
- At the sprint boundary, S merges passing PRs in dependency order, resolves integration issues with the owner, and posts the new `main` commit used by the next sprint.
- Never push directly to shared `main`. Do not force-push shared branches. Keep secrets, local `.env` files, and real personal data out of commits.

Each task's checklist uses these two states:

```text
- [ ] PR uploaded, PR URL recorded, and required checks pass (task owner)
- [ ] Reviewed and merged to main (S/reviewer)
```

Tests: valid model round-trip; reject invalid confidence, price/cost, and lifecycle state; initialize an empty test database and load fixtures. |

# Atlas Commerce Agent — Demo and Test Plan

## Demonstration story

Use fictional regions and products so the result is reproducible and safe to share.

The main demo is a UML sequence model:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor Operator
    participant UI as Dashboard
    participant CFO as cfo.ai
    participant Worker as Autonomous worker
    participant Ranker as Recommendation service
    participant Logs as neatlogs
    participant Entire as Entire evidence

    Operator->>UI: Submit candidate region
    UI->>CFO: Request base/growth/downside assessment
    CFO-->>UI: Viability and opportunity-cost outputs
    Operator->>UI: Approve region
    UI->>Worker: Activate region
    Worker->>Logs: Trace initial recommendation run
    UI-->>Operator: Show initial top-five products
    Worker->>Worker: Consume synthetic festival signal
    Worker->>Ranker: Propose bounded weight update
    Ranker-->>Worker: Candidate before/after rankings
    Worker->>Logs: Record signal, weights, and evaluation
    alt Candidate passes policy, quality, and finance checks
        Worker->>Ranker: Activate recommendation version
        UI-->>Operator: Show changed products and explanations
    else Candidate fails a check
        Worker->>Ranker: Preserve active version
        UI-->>Operator: Show rejection and rollback status
    end
    Entire-->>Operator: Show development checkpoint evidence
```

### Scenario A — region evaluation and activation

1. Open the dashboard with two active regions and one candidate region.
2. Submit the candidate region with traffic, conversion, margin, campaign cost, and data-availability assumptions.
3. Run the financial assessment.
4. Show cfo.ai base, growth, and downside scenarios.
5. Show the viability score, expected profit, and opportunity cost.
6. Approve the region.
7. Show the region entering `active` with a default recommendation profile.
8. Pause and resume the region, then confirm paused regions are skipped by worker runs.

### Scenario B — autonomous update changes products

1. Display the region's current top-five products.
2. Inject a timestamped synthetic festival signal.
3. Run the autonomous cycle.
4. Show research output, normalized topics, confidence, and evidence.
5. Show the old and candidate weights.
6. Show products promoted and demoted.
7. Show the new top-five products in the storefront preview.
8. Show the neatlogs trace containing the cycle and recommendation update.
9. Roll back to the parent version and show the active top five returning to its prior state.

After a signal is consumed, the dashboard shows zero pending signals and disables
the one-region run button. Add fresh synthetic evidence before starting another
cycle. A no-signal cycle is a no-op, not a successful recommendation update.

### Confidence sensitivity check

Use Aspen Ridge so the Cedar fixture signal is not mixed into the experiment.
Reset before each trial, submit one `festival` signal with the same evidence,
and compare confidence `0.65`, `0.70`, and `0.80`. The first is rejected by the
confidence gate, `0.70` should activate and bring LED String Lights into the
top five, and `0.80` should propose a larger change that the simulated profit
guardrail rejects. Identical synthetic submissions reuse one source ID; change
the evidence excerpt when you intend to add a genuinely separate observation.

### Scenario C — rejected update and recovery

1. Inject a low-confidence or low-margin signal.
2. Run the autonomous cycle.
3. Show that the candidate version fails a finance, quality, or policy check.
4. Keep the active recommendation version unchanged.
5. Show the rejection in the UI and neatlogs.
6. Confirm that the next cycle can continue.

### Scenario E — operator replay and reset

1. Select a saved cycle from Activity & evidence and replay its exact signal IDs.
2. Confirm replay creates a new cycle record and leaves prior history intact.
3. Reset the workspace from Settings and confirm fixtures restore the initial state.

The update outcome is a UML state model:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> ActiveVersion
    ActiveVersion --> CandidateVersion: actionable signal
    CandidateVersion --> Evaluating: candidate stored
    Evaluating --> Activated: policy, quality, and finance pass
    Evaluating --> Rejected: any check fails
    Activated --> ActiveVersion: new version becomes active
    Rejected --> ActiveVersion: preserve last known-good version
    ActiveVersion --> RolledBack: post-activation regression
    RolledBack --> ActiveVersion: restore parent version
```

### Scenario D — Entire development evidence

Show:

- the project `AGENTS.md` and planning documents supplied to the coding agent;
- repository graph/context output where available;
- a checkpoint for the first implementation;
- a later checkpoint tied to a fix or improvement;
- the commit or checkpoint references in `docs/evidence.md`.

## Manual verification checklist

- A new region cannot become active without approval.
- An already active region can process a routine update without approval.
- A duplicate source record is processed only once.
- A stale event does not produce a new update.
- A temporary event boost expires.
- A disallowed product never appears in the final ranking.
- An out-of-stock product never appears in the final ranking.
- A candidate update cannot exceed the configured weight-change limit.
- A failed evaluation leaves the active version unchanged.
- A failed region cycle does not prevent another region from running.
- Recommendation score breakdowns explain before/after rank movement.
- Simulated sales use the same customer cohort for active and candidate comparisons.
- A cfo.ai outage is shown as degraded/fallback, not falsely reported as success.
- Missing neatlogs credentials make integration status explicit.
- A paused or archived region is never processed by the all-region worker.
- A replay creates a new cycle and keeps the source cycle immutable.
- Reset clears local operator history and restores the checked-in fixture set.
- All secrets are absent from source, fixtures, logs, and evidence.

"""Deterministic simulated finance and an explicit cfo.ai import boundary."""

from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation, localcontext
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Annotated, Any, Literal

import neatlogs
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator, model_validator

Money = Annotated[Decimal, Field(ge=0, allow_inf_nan=False)]
Rate = Annotated[Decimal, Field(ge=0, le=1, allow_inf_nan=False)]
Finite = Annotated[Decimal, Field(allow_inf_nan=False)]


class FinanceInputs(BaseModel):
    """Monthly synthetic assumptions, shared by local and provider models."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    monthly_traffic: int = Field(default=50000, ge=0)
    conversion_rate: Rate = Decimal("0.025")
    average_order_value: Money = Decimal("85")
    product_cost_per_order: Money = Decimal("45")
    fulfillment_cost_per_order: Money = Decimal("12")
    campaign_cost: Money = Decimal("15000")
    inference_cost: Money = Decimal("3000")
    infrastructure_cost: Money = Decimal("4500")
    cash_balance: Money = Decimal("100000")
    opportunity_cost: Money = Decimal("2000")


class ScenarioResult(BaseModel):
    """Simulated monthly economics; undefined ratios are represented as null."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    name: Literal["base", "growth", "downside"]
    orders: Money
    revenue: Money
    product_cost: Money
    fulfillment_cost: Money
    gross_profit: Finite
    gross_margin: Finite | None
    operating_cost: Money
    profit: Finite
    campaign_roi: Finite | None
    runway_months: Money | None
    opportunity_adjusted_profit: Finite


class FinanceReport(BaseModel):
    """Honest provenance and a local decision, never an activation command."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    status: Literal["degraded"] = "degraded"
    source: Literal["local_simulation"] = "local_simulation"
    reason: str = "cfo.ai unavailable: no authenticated model/scenario read verified."
    assumptions: FinanceInputs
    scenarios: list[ScenarioResult]
    recommendation: Literal["approve", "reject"]
    simulated: Literal[True] = True


class CfoScenarioImport(BaseModel):
    """Validated cfo.ai scenario export; validation is not live verification."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="allow", populate_by_name=True)
    workspace_id: str | None = None
    region_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
    model_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
    scenario_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
    source_url: str = Field(min_length=1)
    assumptions: dict[str, Any] | FinanceInputs
    result: dict[str, Any] | ScenarioResult

    @field_validator("assumptions", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def parse_local_assumptions(cls, value: Any) -> Any:
        """Keep round-trips of the app's pre-existing local import shape."""
        if isinstance(value, dict) and "average_order_value" in value and "campaign_cost" in value:
            return FinanceInputs.model_validate(value)
        return value

    @field_validator("result", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def parse_local_result(cls, value: Any) -> Any:
        """Keep round-trips of the app's existing scenario result shape."""
        if isinstance(value, dict) and value.get("name") in {"base", "growth", "downside"}:
            return ScenarioResult.model_validate(value)
        return value

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_financial_payload(self) -> "CfoScenarioImport":
        """Reject incomplete or non-finite cfo.ai assumptions and outputs."""
        if isinstance(self.assumptions, FinanceInputs) and isinstance(self.result, ScenarioResult):
            return self

        assumptions = self.assumptions
        result = self.result
        if not isinstance(assumptions, dict) or not isinstance(result, dict):
            raise ValueError("assumptions and result must use one supported finance schema")

        assumption_aliases = {
            "monthly_traffic": ("monthly_traffic",),
            "conversion_rate": ("conversion_rate",),
            "average_order_value": ("avg_order_value", "average_order_value"),
            "product_cost_per_order": ("product_cost_per_order",),
            "fulfillment_cost_per_order": ("fulfillment_cost_per_order",),
            "campaign_cost": ("campaign_cost_monthly", "campaign_cost"),
            "inference_cost": ("inference_cost_monthly", "inference_cost"),
            "infrastructure_cost": ("infrastructure_cost_monthly", "infrastructure_cost"),
            "cash_balance": ("cash_balance",),
        }
        values: dict[str, Any] = {}
        for field_name, aliases in assumption_aliases.items():
            value = next((assumptions[key] for key in aliases if key in assumptions), None)
            if value is None:
                raise ValueError(f"cfo.ai assumptions missing {field_name}")
            values[field_name] = value

        for field_name, value in values.items():
            number = _finite_decimal(value, f"assumptions.{field_name}")
            if number < 0:
                raise ValueError(f"assumptions.{field_name} must be non-negative")
        if _finite_decimal(values["conversion_rate"], "assumptions.conversion_rate") > 1:
            raise ValueError("assumptions.conversion_rate must be at most 1")
        traffic = _finite_decimal(values["monthly_traffic"], "assumptions.monthly_traffic")
        if traffic != traffic.to_integral_value():
            raise ValueError("assumptions.monthly_traffic must be an integer")

        required_outputs = {
            "revenue", "product_cost", "fulfillment_cost", "gross_profit",
            "gross_margin", "operating_cost", "profit", "campaign_roi",
            "runway_months", "opportunity_adjusted_profit",
        }
        if "scenario_name" not in result and "name" not in result:
            raise ValueError("cfo.ai result missing scenario_name")
        missing = required_outputs.difference(result)
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"cfo.ai result missing required outputs: {', '.join(sorted(missing))}")
        for field_name in required_outputs:
            value = result[field_name]
            if value is None and field_name in {"gross_margin", "campaign_roi", "runway_months", "opportunity_adjusted_profit"}:
                continue
            _finite_decimal(value, f"result.{field_name}")
        return self

    @classmethod
    def validate_payload(cls, payload: object) -> "CfoScenarioImport":
        """Validate an imported object using this model's strict boundary."""
        return cls.model_validate(payload)


def read_cfo_export(path: Path) -> CfoScenarioImport:
    """Validate operator-supplied JSON; never infer that MCP is authenticated."""
    return CfoScenarioImport.model_validate_json(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def _finite_decimal(value: Any, field_name: str) -> Decimal:
    """Parse one finite numeric value for the cfo.ai import boundary."""
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        raise ValueError(f"{field_name} must be numeric")
    try:
        number = Decimal(str(value))
    except (InvalidOperation, ValueError):
        raise ValueError(f"{field_name} must be numeric") from None
    if not number.is_finite():
        raise ValueError(f"{field_name} must be finite")
    return number


@neatlogs.span(kind="CHAIN", name="simulate_financial_scenarios")
def assess_finance(inputs: FinanceInputs) -> FinanceReport:
    """Compare three deterministic scenarios with no network or activation."""
    scenarios = []
    with localcontext() as context:
        context.prec = 28
        for name, multiplier in (
            ("base", Decimal("1")),
            ("growth", Decimal("1.25")),
            ("downside", Decimal("0.75")),
        ):
            orders = inputs.monthly_traffic * inputs.conversion_rate * multiplier
            revenue = orders * inputs.average_order_value
            product_cost = orders * inputs.product_cost_per_order
            fulfillment = orders * inputs.fulfillment_cost_per_order
            gross = revenue - product_cost - fulfillment
            operating = inputs.campaign_cost + inputs.inference_cost + inputs.infrastructure_cost
            profit = gross - operating
            scenarios.append(ScenarioResult(
                name=name, orders=orders, revenue=revenue, product_cost=product_cost,
                fulfillment_cost=fulfillment, gross_profit=gross,
                gross_margin=gross / revenue if revenue else None,
                operating_cost=operating, profit=profit,
                campaign_roi=(gross - inputs.campaign_cost) / inputs.campaign_cost
                if inputs.campaign_cost else None,
                runway_months=inputs.cash_balance / -profit if profit < 0 else None,
                opportunity_adjusted_profit=profit - inputs.opportunity_cost,
            ))
    base = scenarios[0]
    return FinanceReport(
        assumptions=inputs, scenarios=scenarios,
        recommendation="approve" if (
            base.opportunity_adjusted_profit > 0
            and base.gross_margin is not None and base.gross_margin >= Decimal("0.2")
        ) else "reject",
    )

import logging
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

from adaptive_commerce.agents import PersistedSignalSource, SignalSource
from adaptive_commerce.agents.signals import NormalizedSignal
from adaptive_commerce.application.profile_updates import propose_profile_update
from adaptive_commerce.domain import (

)
from adaptive_commerce.integrations.observability import trace_step
from adaptive_commerce.persistence import Repository, connect

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class CycleResult(BaseModel):
    """Operator-facing result for one durable regional cycle."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    cycle: UpdateCycle
    before_version_id: str | None = None
    after_version_id: str | None = None
    promoted: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    demoted: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    before: list[dict[str, Any]] = Field(default_factory=list)
    after: list[dict[str, Any]] = Field(default_factory=list)
    metrics: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    replay_of: str | None = None


class EvaluationPolicy(BaseModel):
    """Minimum deterministic quality and profit retention for activation."""

    min_profit_retention: Decimal = Field(default=Decimal("0.85"), ge=0, le=1)
    min_relevance_delta: Decimal = Field(default=Decimal("0"), ge=0)


def run_region_cycle(
    path: Path,
    region_id: str,
    *,
    now: datetime | None = None,
    cycle_id: str | None = None,
    replay_signal_ids: list[str] | None = None,
    replay_of: str | None = None,
    signal_source: SignalSource | None = None,
    evaluation_policy: EvaluationPolicy | None = None,
) -> CycleResult:
    """Run one idempotent update cycle for an active region.

    Signal consumption, cycle outcome, candidate version, event windows, and
    activation are committed together. Failures are recorded separately while
    leaving the active version and unconsumed signals intact.
    """
    at = now or datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    if at.tzinfo is None or at.utcoffset() is None:
        raise ValueError("now must be timezone-aware")
    stable_cycle_id = cycle_id or str(uuid4())
    try:
        with trace_step("WORKFLOW", "regional_update_cycle", region_id=region_id,
                        cycle_id=stable_cycle_id) as span:
            result = _run_cycle_transaction(
                path, region_id, at, stable_cycle_id,
                replay_signal_ids=replay_signal_ids, replay_of=replay_of,
                signal_source=signal_source,
                evaluation_policy=evaluation_policy or EvaluationPolicy(),
            )
            span.set_attribute("atlas.result_status", result.cycle.status.value)
            span.set_attribute("atlas.activation_status", "activated" if result.after_version_id != result.before_version_id else "unchanged")
            logger.info("regional_cycle_finished", extra={
                "region_id": region_id, "cycle_id": stable_cycle_id,
                "result_status": result.cycle.status.value,
            })
            return result
    except Exception as error:
        _record_failure(path, region_id, stable_cycle_id, at, error)
        logger.exception("regional_cycle_failed", extra={
            "region_id": region_id, "cycle_id": stable_cycle_id,
            "result_status": "failed",
        })
        raise


def _run_cycle_transaction(
    path: Path,
    region_id: str,
    now: datetime,
    cycle_id: str,
    *,
    replay_signal_ids: list[str] | None,
    replay_of: str | None,
    signal_source: SignalSource | None,
    evaluation_policy: EvaluationPolicy,
) -> CycleResult:
    with connect(path) as conn:
        repository = Repository(conn)
        previous = repository.get_update_cycle(cycle_id)
        if previous is not None:
            return _result_from_cycle(previous)
        region = repository.get_region(region_id)
        if region is None or region.state is not RegionState.active:
            raise ValueError("regional cycles require an active region")
        active = repository.get_active_profile(region_id)
        active_version = repository.get_active_version(region_id)
        if active is None or active_version is None:
            raise ValueError("active region has no recommendation profile")
        with trace_step("TOOL", "signal_fetch", region_id=region_id,
                        cycle_id=cycle_id) as span:
            signals = (
                [repository.get_signal(item) for item in replay_signal_ids]
                if replay_signal_ids is not None
                else (signal_source or PersistedSignalSource()).fetch_unprocessed(repository, region_id)
            )
            span.set_attribute("atlas.signal_count", len(signals))
        if any(signal is None or signal.region_id != region_id for signal in signals):
            raise ValueError("cycle signal is missing or belongs to another region")
        concrete_signals = [signal for signal in signals if signal is not None]
        with trace_step("CHAIN", "signal_normalization", region_id=region_id,
                        cycle_id=cycle_id) as span:
            normalized = [
                NormalizedSignal(
                    signal=signal,
                    topic_impacts={topic: Decimal("1") for topic in signal.topics},
                )
                for signal in concrete_signals
            ]
            span.set_attribute("atlas.normalized_count", len(normalized))

        candidate_version_id = f"v-{region_id}-{uuid4().hex[:10]}"
        with trace_step("GUARDRAIL", "signal_policy_result", region_id=region_id,
                        cycle_id=cycle_id, version_id=candidate_version_id) as span:
            proposal = propose_profile_update(
                active, normalized, now=now, candidate_version_id=candidate_version_id,
                cycle_id=cycle_id,
            )
            span.set_attribute("atlas.accepted_count", len(proposal.accepted_signal_ids))
            span.set_attribute("atlas.rejected_count", len(proposal.rejections))
            span.set_attribute("atlas.changed_topic_count", len(proposal.changes))
            span.set_attribute("atlas.result_status", "candidate" if proposal.changed else "unchanged")
        cycle = UpdateCycle(
            id=cycle_id,
            region_id=region_id,
            signal_ids=[signal.id for signal in concrete_signals],
            proposed_changes=proposal.changes or None,
            status=UpdateCycleStatus.evaluating,
            created_at=now,
        )
        repository.create_update_cycle(cycle)

        if not proposal.changed:
            evaluation = {
                "result": "no_actionable_change",
                "rejections": [item.model_dump(mode="json") for item in proposal.rejections],
                "before_version_id": active.active_version_id,
                "after_version_id": active.active_version_id,
                "replay_of": replay_of,
                "simulated": True,
            }
            final = cycle.model_copy(update={
                "status": UpdateCycleStatus.rejected,
                "rejection_reason": "no_actionable_signals",
                "evaluation": evaluation,
                "finished_at": now,
            })
            repository.update_update_cycle(final)
            if not replay_signal_ids:
                repository.mark_signals_processed(final.signal_ids, cycle_id)
            return CycleResult(cycle=final, before_version_id=active.active_version_id,
                               after_version_id=active.active_version_id,
                               metrics=evaluation, replay_of=replay_of)

        candidate = RecommendationVersion(
            id=candidate_version_id,
            region_id=region_id,
            parent_id=active.active_version_id,
            weights=proposal.candidate_profile.weights,
            status=VersionStatus.candidate,
            created_at=now,
        )
        repository.create_recommendation_version(candidate)
        for event in proposal.event_windows:
            repository.create_event_window(event)

        products = [RankingProduct.model_validate(item)
                    for item in repository.get_products_for_ranking(region_id)]
        policy = RankingPolicy.model_validate(repository.get_ranking_policy(region_id))
        event_windows = [RankingEvent.model_validate(item)
                         for item in repository.get_active_events(region_id, now.isoformat())]
        active_profile = RankingProfile.model_validate(active)
        candidate_profile = RankingProfile.model_validate(proposal.candidate_profile)
        with trace_step("CHAIN", "candidate_comparison_ranking", region_id=region_id,
                        cycle_id=cycle_id, version_id=candidate_version_id,
                        attributes={"product_count": len(products)}):
            before = rank_products(products, active_profile, now=now, policy=policy,
                                   events=event_windows, cycle_id=cycle_id)
            after = rank_products(products, candidate_profile, now=now, policy=policy,
                                  events=event_windows, cycle_id=cycle_id)
        with trace_step("EVALUATOR", "same_cohort_comparison", region_id=region_id,
                        cycle_id=cycle_id, version_id=candidate_version_id) as span:
            metrics = _evaluate_same_cohort(before, after, products, active.weights,
                                            proposal.changes, normalized)
            accepted = metrics["candidate_relevance"] >= (
                metrics["active_relevance"] + float(evaluation_policy.min_relevance_delta)
            ) and metrics["candidate_profit"] >= (
                metrics["active_profit"] * float(evaluation_policy.min_profit_retention)
            )
            span.set_attribute("atlas.policy_passed", accepted)
            span.set_attribute("atlas.result_status", "approved" if accepted else "rejected")
        metrics["policy_passed"] = accepted
        metrics["min_profit_retention"] = str(evaluation_policy.min_profit_retention)
        metrics["min_relevance_delta"] = str(evaluation_policy.min_relevance_delta)
        metrics["simulated"] = True
        metrics["cohort"] = "fixed regional demand cohort, same for active and candidate"
        metrics["rejections"] = [item.model_dump(mode="json") for item in proposal.rejections]
        old_ranks = {item.product_id: item.rank for item in before}
        new_ranks = {item.product_id: item.rank for item in after}
        promoted = [item.product_id for item in after
                    if item.product_id not in old_ranks or item.rank < old_ranks[item.product_id]]
        demoted = [item.product_id for item in before
                   if item.product_id not in new_ranks or item.rank > new_ranks[item.product_id]]
        if accepted:
            if not repository.set_active_version(region_id, candidate_version_id):
                raise RuntimeError("candidate activation failed")
            status = UpdateCycleStatus.activated
            reason = None
            after_version_id = candidate_version_id
        else:
            repository.reject_recommendation_version(candidate_version_id)
            status = UpdateCycleStatus.rejected
            reason = "evaluation_gate_failed"
            after_version_id = active.active_version_id
        with trace_step("CHAIN", "recommendation_version_outcome", region_id=region_id,
                        cycle_id=cycle_id, version_id=candidate_version_id,
                        attributes={"result_status": "activated" if accepted else "rejected"}):
            pass
        metrics.update({
            "before_version_id": active.active_version_id,
            "after_version_id": after_version_id,
            "before": [item.model_dump(mode="json") for item in before],
            "after": [item.model_dump(mode="json") for item in after],
            "promoted": promoted if accepted else [],
            "demoted": demoted if accepted else [],
            "replay_of": replay_of,
        })
        final = cycle.model_copy(update={
            "status": status,
            "rejection_reason": reason,
            "evaluation": metrics,
            "finished_at": now,
        })
        repository.update_update_cycle(final)
        if not replay_signal_ids:
            repository.mark_signals_processed(final.signal_ids, cycle_id)
        return CycleResult(
            cycle=final,
            before_version_id=active.active_version_id,
            after_version_id=after_version_id,
            promoted=promoted if accepted else [],
            demoted=demoted if accepted else [],
            before=[item.model_dump(mode="json") for item in before],
            after=[item.model_dump(mode="json") for item in after],
            metrics=metrics,
            replay_of=replay_of,
        )
